text: Process Canvas ports (emits, dataFlow, channels, parentMemberId, stage) are declarative-only: the agent still applies the label at runtime, and graph edges are derived from these ports — so dropping a port entry corrupts the model/graph without necessarily changing runtime routing.

Recovering interrupted prior-run work: a crashed/interrupted run may leave an issue's WIP in a git STASH (not only in the working tree or a bare branch) — run 'git stash list' before assuming work was reverted/lost. Note 'git checkout stash@{N} -- <files>' STAGES those files, so a later gh-as-agent commit of other work sweeps them in; unstash into a scratch area or reset the index if you need separate commits.

Lucide role-template icons live in shared admin-console/src/components/role-icons.js (ROLE_ICONS map + roleIcon(name) helper, default User); TeamSetup.jsx and ProcessCanvas.jsx AddRoleDialog both import it — don't re-duplicate the map (created in PR #593 for #586 AC1).
GitHub issues/tickets in 314092_agent-execution-environment are always authored in English, even when the requesting human chats in another language (e.g. German).

To integration-test a commit-making CLI's git behaviour (knowledge/gh-as-agent) without an ambient identity, run the real CLI as a subprocess inside a temp `git init` repo with a stripped identity: HOME=empty tmp dir, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/SYSTEM=os.devnull, and GIT_AUTHOR/COMMITTER_NAME/EMAIL popped from env.

When a CLI tool wraps a git commit, extract identity args into a pure `build_commit_args()`-style helper so unit tests can assert the inline `-c user.name/user.email` flags without running git; the integration test then runs the full CLI against a stripped-identity env to close the gap.

buildAgentClaudeMd has TWO call sites whose output must stay byte-identical — saveAgentPrompt (seed) and the /internal/agents/:id/prompt-preview endpoint; any new per-agent opt (skills, skillDescriptions, knowledgeDigestRef) MUST be threaded through both or the preview diverges from what's seeded.

When a prompt-assembly.js enrichment reads data from disk, the I/O helper belongs in orchestrator.js (fail-soft, try/catch per item) while the pure renderer in prompt-assembly.js stays fs-free and accepts the data as a caller-supplied map — see agentSkillDescriptions + skillsSection pattern in PR #618.

For AC6 (preview == seed) in CLAUDE.md composition features: both `saveAgentPrompt` and the `/internal/agents/:id/prompt-preview` endpoint must be updated to pass the same enrichment data to buildAgentClaudeMd — verify both call sites in every prompt-assembly PR.

When a dialog has single vs multi-item phrasing, use a derived boolean flag (e.g. `single = aggregated && count <= 1`) to branch copy only — leave controls, submit logic, and checkbox behaviour untouched; the flag is purely presentational.

When threading graph-node data from a section component into a dialog (e.g. teamSkills for extend-target picker), pass it as a second argument to the callback prop (onReviewSuggestion(s, skills)) and store it on the state object that opens the dialog — single source of truth, no separate fetch needed.

The skill.json startup backfill (and any bulk write to the GLOBAL skill pool) MUST live in admin-console, not the orchestrator: the orchestrator mounts /template-workspace (=/pool/skills) READ-ONLY, while admin-console mounts /pool RW. Both mount /workspace (team+agent skills) RW. So orchestrator can only stamp team-tier skills (_teamSkillDir) and agent dirs.

Two-sided module pattern (skill-manifest, knowledge-digest): when reviewing, run 'node --test' on BOTH test suites and verify byte-identical guard (test case that diffs the two files) passes — this is the only automated drift detector between admin-console and orchestrator copies.

skill-manifest.js copy semantics: stampSkillCopy (promote/lift/share) discards the cpSync-dragged skill.json before re-stamping (fresh v1 chain + origin); stampSkill (import, edit, create) reads any existing manifest and continues the chain — concept §3.1 / §3.5. Verify correct choice when reviewing any new copy-creating path.

Adding an optional field to the two-sided knowledge store (orchestrator/knowledge-store.js + agent-image/scripts/knowledge) stays JSONL byte-identical iff appended LAST in KEY_ORDER on BOTH mirrors and only emitted when a non-empty trimmed string; an absent field then serializes exactly as before, so the digest (reads text only) is provably unchanged. Assert with a 'field absent unless supplied round-trips identical' test on both the JS (node --test) and Python (test_knowledge.py) suites.

Route-level display overlay pattern in admin-console/api/api.js: compute read-time-only display fields (e.g. augmentDisplaySummary, sibling of augmentDigestInclusion) in the /api/knowledge/graph route AFTER the pure graph builder, so the pure builder stays entries+skills-only and never depends on LLM/heuristic display logic. Persist only authoritative values (real LLM summaries) via the canonical overlay in runConvergenceCollector/_serializeCanonicalKind, carried forward across convergence only while the entry text is unchanged (text edit -> regenerate).

When a new optional field is added to a two-sided JS+Python KB store, the KEY_ORDER, makeKnowledgeEntry/build_entry, and validateKnowledgeEntry must all be updated in BOTH mirrors and both cross-runtime GOLDEN tests must pass — no summary field emitted when absent means serialisation is byte-identical to pre-PR output.

Carry-forward pattern for re-projection-derived fields (summary, #635): read prior canonical files before re-projecting, carry each entry's field forward only when prev.text === e.text, so a text change drops the stale field and triggers regeneration on the next write pass.

Skill move-transfer strand guard (skill-transfer #626): a move to GLOBAL never strands (universal fallback remains); a move to a TEAM tier can orphan grantees OUTSIDE that team -> POST /api/skills/transfer returns 409 with the agent-id list unless force:true (or a global copy of the name still exists). Move always archives the source to /workspace/skill-archive/<tierSeg>/<name>-<hash>-<ts>/ before deleting.

When a PR adds a new UI action that supersedes an existing button, the old button must be removed in the same PR — leaving both co-existing fails the 'no-provenance paths gone from UI' criterion and creates a confusing dual-action UI (seen in PR #638 team→global: two buttons, one without provenance).

When a PR introduces an engine that supersedes old endpoints, the Code Reviewer treats ANY surviving old UI call to the deprecated endpoint as an AC violation (esp. no-provenance paths) — grep the .jsx for the deprecated endpoint URLs, remove the button AND its wrapper fn, not just the backend.

CodeQL 'uncontrolled data used in path expression' on admin-console skill endpoints clears by routing the filesystem probe through the containment-guarded resolver (transferSkillExistsAt / resolveTransferSkillDir, which use path.resolve+path.relative) — a raw path.join on an already-SKILL_NAME_RE-validated name still trips the query; do NOT add redundant validation.

Reworker: on every wake compare the SHA the latest review examined (review body / git show -s --format=%ci) against current branch HEAD before re-doing work — a fix that lands seconds before the revisions-required label still counts; if HEAD already resolves the findings, re-verify (grep deprecated symbols + run tests) and re-hand-back with a PR comment flagging the timing race instead of re-editing.

When reviewing a skill-tier engine PR (#626 pattern), always check KnowledgeFlow.jsx fetch() calls — the ShareDialog and lift path use /api/knowledge/share-to-team and /api/knowledge/promote which are separate from /api/skills/transfer; the issue key-files list is the reliable guide to which files must be changed.

Reworker: when a Code Reviewer promotes a previously-declared-NON-blocking item to a blocker across review passes AND the requested fix would regress functionality, escalate with a blocking PR comment quoting the earlier pass rather than silently complying; fix any clean sibling items but do NOT re-apply ready-for-review while the contested blocker is open.

Reworker: when escalating a PR to a human (contradictory/impossible/product-decision review feedback), apply the 'human-decision-required' label (magenta #5319E7, created in 314092 repo 2026-07-16) to the PR in addition to the blocking comment — do NOT re-apply ready-for-review while it is set, and remove it once the question is resolved and the PR is handed back. Label makes the paused-for-human state visible in the PR list.

In process-template bundles, the CI lint guard (process-template-registry.test.js 'render with no error/warning lints') builds the graph ONLY from roles' emits/github/channels/triggers — NOT from the labels[] registry; adding/removing a labels entry is lint-safe as long as the bundle still passes validateProcessTemplate (which only checks labels is an array). The gate-violation lint fires only on an agent's emits of a human:*-PREFIXED label.

Label-schema convention for a 'pause-for-human' signal that an AGENT applies (e.g. human-decision-required in core-sdlc.json): { humanGate: false, brake: true } — brake=pauses the loop (like hold/needs:human), humanGate:false because the agent (not a human) sets it.

core-sdlc.json label schema: humanGate=true means a human applies the label (e.g. 'ready'); humanGate=false means an agent applies it; brake=true means the label pauses the automated loop pending a human decision (e.g. 'human-decision-required'); brake=false means it is a routing signal only.

Skill deletion (skill-deletion.js #627): DELETE /api/skills/:name guards all tiers uniformly (409 lists blocking constructs), cascade:true deactivates blocking grants then deletes; the snapshot MUST be taken BEFORE cascade (an agent-tier cascade removes the very dir) and rolled back on a refused 409 delete so a blocked attempt leaves no orphan archive. Team Admin can delete a team skill without System Admin (permitDeletion team tier).

Skill archive layout (#627): every delete snapshots to /workspace/skill-archive/<tierSeg>/<name>-<hash>-<ts>/ + an archive-meta.json sidecar (same dir layout skill-transfer's MOVE writes — moved+deleted skills share ONE restore surface; deliberately a directory, NOT the ZIP the concept §3.3 wording implies). Restore via POST /api/skills/archive/restore excludes archive-meta.json from the restored dir; prune via planArchivePrune (pure, default 90d, System-Admin only).

When an issue lists KnowledgeFlow.jsx as a key file alongside a permission-gating AC for Team Admins, verify BOTH the backend gate AND the frontend route guard — AdminRoute (user.admin = sysadmin/envAdmin only) blocks Team Admins from SkillsRegistry; the fix belongs in either the route or KnowledgeFlow.jsx.

Cold-nav-safe deep-link into agent chat: navigate to /chats/<agentId>?session=<correlationId> (a bookmarkable query param, not router state); AgentChat.jsx consumes it via useSearchParams only after the agent list has loaded + agent exists (consumedSessionRef guards re-fire), then strips the param with setSearchParams(replace:true). Reuse the existing railTabRequest {tab,ts} mechanism (thread a sibling sessionSelectRequest {correlationId,ts} down AgentChat->RightRail(selectRequest)->SessionsPanel) rather than inventing a parallel one (PR #645, issue #642 AC4/AC7).
